Arsenal moved to the top of the Premier League with their first win at Liverpool in 14 years as Kai Havertz’s early strike secured a 1-0 victory for the Gunners. The defending champions were made to suffer after the German’s 16th-minute opener but held out for what could be a telling win in their quest to retain the title. Arsenal climbed three points clear of Manchester City at the top of the table. But with City expected to be hit with a severe points penalty, unless they can overturn a guilty verdict on more than 100 charges of breaking Premier League rules, Arsenal dealt a huge blow to their most likely rivals for the title. Liverpool produced arguably their best spell of Andoni Iraola’s early months in charge with a blistering 30 minutes after conceding, but failed to take their chances as the Spaniard suffered just his second defeat in 14 games since arriving from Bournemouth. Mikel Arteta was stinging in his criticism of the Arsenal side that crashed out to fourth-tier Fleetwood on Tuesday in one of the biggest ever League Cup shocks. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources The Arsenal boss got the response he desired with a strong start from the champions. Havertz was one of the biggest culprits for wasting chances in midweek but made amends with a simple finish from Declan Rice’s precise low cross. The early goal lit the touchpaper for a pulsating first 45 minutes as Liverpool roared back. Iraola and Arteta played together as boys for Basque side Antiguoko Kirol Elkartea. Arteta’s old friend gave his side one of the most uncomfortable afternoons they have experienced in recent seasons as Arsenal’s rock-solid defence was left clinging on for half-time. All of Liverpool’s three £100 million-plus ($134 million) forwards started together, and there are signs the relationship between Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola is beginning to flourish. Isak did Arsenal a favour by not going down as he was pulled back by Jurrien Timber when he failed to connect with a delivery from Barcola. The visitors still had chances on the counter-attack as Bruno Guimaraes pulled a shot just wide before Timber inadvertently blocked Noni Madueke’s ball across goal with Havertz waiting to apply the finish. At the other end, Wirtz curled a free-kick onto the bar from a narrow angle, and Alexis Mac Allister should have buried a header rather than finding the stand behind David Raya’s goal. Half-time allowed Arsenal the chance to reset and take the wind out of Liverpool’s sails as Iraola’s men tired in the second period. Alisson Becker produced a stunning save to turn Christos Tzolis’s shot behind, with the ball arrowing into the bottom corner, to keep Liverpool in the game. That intervention counted for little as Arsenal rode out the closing stages to register another clean sheet and an eighth win in nine league games. Defeat leaves fifth-placed Liverpool nine points adrift of the leaders and already facing a mountain to climb to get back into the title race. AFP Kindly share this story:
